# Plan an observatory night across the scheduler, Gantt and task board

## Visitor outcome
Run an observing night at Meridian Observatory. A science exposure is competing for a telescope, its prerequisites affect its observing window, and the crew controls clearance. A visitor can inspect the plan, make decisions in three native v14 widgets and see the same campaign change across them. Release showcase for #21140 and #20874.

## Delivery
Use real `Neo.scheduler.Container` resource bookings, `Neo.gantt.Container` tasks and dependency cascades, and `Neo.board.Container` status cards. A bounded simulated night supplies more than one program and telescope. Project the current plan into a window/conflict readout that explains what will happen. Workstation Planning #21223 is prior art for sharing records across board and scheduler. The broadcast list example #21653 remains an independent example.

## What the visitor decides while holding a card

The touchstone is a four-minute exposure of a simulated two-minute occultation. Two telescopes can catch it with different costs. North collects more samples but occupies a camera needed by a movable mosaic; South preserves that booking at a lower cadence. A late slot misses ingress. The runnable fixture and timing assumptions are in [the design discussion](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/21664). The three-widget baseline below remains useful even before all the cross-widget interactions land.

## Flagship acceptance
- [ ] During one uninterrupted drag from the native Board, compare two real Scheduler resource/time targets. The compact verdict, detailed timing and proposed downstream Gantt spans update before release. An incompatible slot identifies its particular constraint. The original card, bookings, task dates and selection stay intact while considering the alternatives.
- [ ] On release, exactly one accepted plan is published across all three widgets. Escape and a stale or refused drop leave committed work intact. Include a keyboard way to compare and confirm, and a reproducible pointer check on stock widgets.
- [ ] The simulated instrument readout shows what those particular timings capture or miss, including whether ingress was recorded. The caption must distinguish predicted data from a completed observation.

## Three-widget baseline
- [ ] The opening identifies an observing target, competing bookings, an observing window and crew clearance; all three widgets are reachable and populated.
- [ ] Moving an exposure to another telescope in the scheduler changes the allocation/conflict outcome and updates the corresponding work item.
- [ ] Editing the time of a prerequisite in the Gantt cascades into the linked exposure and downstream processing; the scheduler and observing-window readout reflect the same dates.
- [ ] Moving a card in the real task board changes crew clearance and the plan's readiness. Resource/time and crew decisions must all hold for a cleared plan, and reversing a decision restores its warning.
- [ ] A fresh/replayed night and the public catalog entry work. A headless browser drives native gestures, inspects underlying records and verifies the result across the views.

## Placement and scope
Standalone example and catalog entry. Keep the science fixtures in the demo. If the native widgets cannot safely supply an interaction, record the reproducible gap on its owning surface. The source-side off-board drop defect is #21662. Broader contracts are open in [the design discussion](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/21664). Current latest-open issue sweep, all-state observatory search, own open assignments, A2A claims, KB and Memory Core checked November 20. The existing planning example and the component-family leaves cover different outcomes.
